newsitem.title: USA: Donations meant for senate races went to gov - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Donations meant for senate races went to gov - NYT.

text.p: Some donations intended to fund Republican senatorial campaigns ended up in the campaign chest of the New York governor, the New York Times reported on Tuesday.

The paper said the donations, including $50,000 from a North Carolina doctor and $20,000 from a Detroit trucking executive, were made to the National Republican Senatorial Committee, which is headed by New York Sen. Alfonse D'Amato.

Instead of reaching any Republican Senate candidates, however, these donations and others went into one of two state-level accounts, including one for the "New York State Victory Committee," the report said.

The report said money from that account was used to make a $1.9 million campaign donation to Gov. George Pataki and $300,000 in donations to finance the elections of three Republicans to the New York Supreme Court.
"There is nothing wrong with what I did," D'Amato told the paper in an interview, although the paper said he acknowledged few donors were told about the check transfers.
"It's not necessary to tell people where their checks went. There is nothing wrong with that. We don't have an obligation to tell people. Money is fungible," the paper quoted the senator as saying.
The report said some of those whose checks were transferred to local races include New York cosmetics executive Ronald Lauder and senior executives of Goldman Sachs.
It said money from companies such as U S West Comunications, Browning-Ferris, Dime Bancorp, PaineWebber and Morgan Stanley intended for Republican senate campaigns also went to local New York races.

The report said the transfer of contributions is not illegal, but said campaign finance experts believe such moves would have violated New York and federal laws if the donations had been made directly.
